title: The stones nobody could lift
style: documentary photograph, limestone quarry, hard Levantine sunlight, muted colour, fine grain, no text, no watermark, no modern objects
negative: text, letters, words, watermark, logo, cartoon, cgi, painting, illustration, modern machinery, tourists

lines.vo: Under a Roman temple in Lebanon sit three blocks no crane today could lift.
lines.image: three colossal limestone blocks in a temple foundation, hard sunlight

lines.vo: Each weighs about eight hundred tons. The one still in the quarry weighs sixteen hundred.
lines.image: an unfinished megalith lying in a limestone quarry
imageCommons: Stone of the Pregnant Woman Baalbek

lines.vo: They were cut from bedrock half a mile uphill from where they sit.
lines.image: a limestone quarry face with cut channels, sloping ground

lines.vo: No pulley of the period could take that load. No rope would hold it.
lines.image: a coil of heavy hemp rope on stone

lines.vo: So the Romans did not lift them. They rolled them.
lines.image: hardwood logs laid in rows on a flat earth road

lines.vo: Hardwood rollers under a timber cradle, and capstans hauling on ropes ahead.
lines.image: a heavy timber frame, thick beams pegged together

lines.vo: Roughly a thousand men on those ropes, moving the block a few feet an hour.
lines.image: a wide dusty haul road under white sun

lines.vo: It took months. The stones were never lifted, only slid, level, on wood.
Not one machine. Sixty thousand man-days, and a road flat enough to hold them.
lines.image: the temple podium at dusk, empty
lines.title: SIXTY THOUSAND
lines.footer: man-days, and no machine at all
